title: Bug in pow() function, setting negative numbers to the power of zero defaults to positive 1
body:
### Tested versions

I only tested in Godot_v4.6.2-stable_win64

### System information

Windows 11 - Godot_v4.6.2

### Issue description

I have a dynamic variable I need incremented by a positive or negative number depending on the positive value of a set integer.

I decided to determine this by saving the integer's value in a variable by setting it to the power of zero, setting the integer to its absolute value to be modified, and multiplying the doctored integer by the variable later. But whenever I ran the following code, it always came up positive:

```gdscript
func _display(label: Label, upgraded: bool):
	var val = pow(adding, 0)
	adding = (abs(adding) + Manager.card_add_increment)
	if upgraded: adding += upgrade
	adding = adding * val
	var a = str(adding)
	if adding > -1: a = "+" + a
	label.text = a
	label.modulate = Color(1, 1, 1)
```

I ended up successfully solving the problem with the following if statement, so it appears to be an issue with the power function.

```gdscript
func _display(label: Label, upgraded: bool):
	var val = 1
	if adding < 0: val = -1
	adding = (abs(adding) + Manager.card_add_increment)
	if upgraded: adding += upgrade
	adding = adding * val
	var a = str(adding)
	if adding > -1: a = "+" + a
	label.text = a
	label.modulate = Color(1, 1, 1)
```

### Steps to reproduce

It should work with just:

```gdscript
print(str(pow(-2, 0)))
```

Any negative number works though, I even tried -1 and it still outputted 1.0

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A, ran in a fresh and separate existing project with multiple numbers and it still happened.
